<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `94a830662475ea64d62096a06e1cbd7e57343965` — the merge of head `f74084f608ea868780a3410ed8838cfb35681059` into base `6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 94a830662475ea64d62096a06e1cbd7e57343965 && git checkout 94a830662475ea64d62096a06e1cbd7e57343965
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 f74084f608ea868780a3410ed8838cfb35681059 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 && git merge --no-ff f74084f608ea868780a3410ed8838cfb35681059

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a9779e0f16e087671077c0d3d53fcc4d89095004`
Local-runs: probe — one worktree at the head (closure built with OS_SKIP_DTS=1): the touched packages' targeted suites, one ablation of the late-install re-judge, and uncommitted scratch cases to confirm the door and store findings before grading them
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (+test), packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts (+match-endpoint test), packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, picklist-resolution.ts, plugin.ts, registry.ts and their picklist / boot-audit / exact-qualifier / bare-name-one-holder family tests, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts (+dataset-holders test), index.ts, protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-qualified-item-read.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-references.integration.test.ts, the two dogfood family tests + read for context: database-loader.ts, memory-loader.ts, protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, package-scoped-read.ts, engine-hooks-and-functions.ts, metadata-facade.ts

### ① Derived judgments
- Declaration lines match rulings 6810963021: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the body and the changeset, with the ADR-0087 marker.
- Probe at head: objectql family + picklist files 348/348; core package-scoped-resolution 29/29; metadata match-endpoint 412/412; metadata-protocol build-probes-dataset-holders 7/7. Not run locally: runtime, cli, dogfood.
- Ablation: with the late-install refusal in `plugin.ts` disabled, both ruling-A order pins go red and the two CONTROLs stay green; restored, 68/68.
- Ruling A (6811306558) holds for the two pinned orders. `findPicklistReferencesBrokenBy` judges the pending view before `registerApp`, the refusal names each reference and both holders, and the tests assert nothing registered.
- Red line 3 (reads): one-holder bare names read as before; the store's one-holder CONTROL covers picklist, mapping and dataset.
- `function` is exempted by name in exactly two pins (slotted superset, exact-qualifier 501); `claimBareNameFunctions` reads the incoming namespace from the installed record.
- Three scratch cases contradict the PR's claims; they are must-fix 1–3 below.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on core, metadata, objectql and metadata-protocol is right for `narrowed`. The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker are present. runtime, cli and dogfood change tests only.

### ③ Boundary flags
- No `packages/spec` file and no governed path in the diff.
- `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json` still names only agent and skill as narrowed. It is outside the diff; flagged for its owner.
- Landing after #32214 and #31696 PR-3 means a new head: the three type sets and these pins are re-reviewed there.
- mapping, dataset and function have no install-door re-judge. A late second holder makes a dependent's read answer 409 naming both at use time: reported, not guessed. Noted, not graded.

### ④ Design judgment
The narrowing does what ADR-0150 D2/D9 says on the pinned paths, and fails on these:

**Must-fix**
1. **Self-extension slips the late-install door.** `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:1016` (`if (own.has(ref.picklist)) return undefined;`, applied to extensions at `:1029`) and `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:10532` skip the incoming package's own extensions. Measured: alpha holds `p1`, and a late install of gamma declaring `p1` plus a `picklistExtensions` entry on `p1` is admitted (main: refused `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`). `findOrphanPicklistExtensions()` then names gamma's extension, and the next cold boot is refused. This breaks ruling A and row 7's "refused at install". Needs a late-order pin.
2. **A late install can silently strip an installed field's options.** `registry.ts:10495` judges each referrer alone; `plugin.ts:1329` names the disagreement only at boot. Measured: alpha owns `alpha_item.s → p1`. A late install or upgrade of gamma that declares its own `p1` and redeclares that field in `objectExtensions` is admitted; served options go from `['alpha_one']` to `[]` with no error and no log. This is the harm ruling A was made for, on another package's field (red line 2).
3. **Undeclared moved answers** (red line 3). `package-slotted-store.ts:111` moves the store contract for picklist, mapping and dataset; the changeset declares only rows 4–6:
   - (a) `unregister(type, NAME, { packageId })` naming a non-holder: FROM item removed TO nothing removed (one-holder move).
   - (b) `unregisterPackage(holder)` after a package-less write over its name: FROM package-less item stays TO removed with the slot (one-holder move).
   - (c) `list(type)` for a two-holder name: FROM the survivor alone TO both (#32151 declared the same line for agent/skill, plus the realtime event kind).
   - (d) A package-less write under a two-holder name: FROM replacing the stored item TO a bare slot, listed, answered by no by-name read.
   - (e) DatabaseLoader for these types: one row per (package, name) with `package_id`, a no-package delete of a two-holder name refused, and rollback by name refused when several slots exist (read, not measured).
   - (f) `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts:163`: a bare read on a registry with `readsByPackage(type) === false`: FROM served TO `501`.
   Each needs a FROM → TO row with its Clause-② arm in the body and changeset, and a pin where none iterates the new types ((a), (b), (e)).

**Should-fix**
- Item seam: `registry.registerItem('picklist', …, 'com.acme.beta')` after seal is admitted beside an installed extension (one orphan measured). Moving the re-judge into the registry closes it with must-fix 1.
- Hot reload: `plugin.ts:1866` re-registers through `registerApp` and bypasses the door. Declare it or cover it.
- Bare engine function read: `ObjectQL#resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry` (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:270-276`) answer the last-registered function, now that two namespaces' holders are admitted.
- `Skills-docs:` should read `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`; the line names `SKILL.md:261` as now false.
- Row 12: state that a widget's dataset held outside the publishing package's closure goes FROM probed TO `widget_not_probed`.

**Nits**: the reworded `describeUnresolvedPicklistReferences` sentence is in the body but not the changeset; the dev report counts 21 build-probe tests where the touched file holds 7.

- **R2-A holds on every named path.** `SchemaRegistry.judgePicklistArrival` (`registry.ts:10762`) is reached from:
  - the install door
  - direct `registerApp`
  - hot reload
  - `registerItem('picklist')`
  - `registerPicklistExtension`
  - `registerObject`

  It judges one pending view, with no own-name shortcut.
  - The four round-1 cases and eleven new scratch cases are refused before anything registers, naming the reference and both holders.

- **R2-B holds.** (a)–(f) are declared with arms; reverting the three store types turns 18 tests red.
- **R2-C is pinned (409 naming both, one-holder CONTROL), but row 19's "no production caller" is false at this head.** See must-fix 2.
- **R2-D:** row 12 and the nits are fixed. `Skills-docs:` still reads `follow-up owed`; the seat rewrites it to `follow-up #32522`.

`minor` on core, metadata, objectql and metadata-protocol is right for `narrowed`. Must-fix 2 adds a runtime source change and a changeset line.

### ③ Boundary flags
- No `packages/spec` file and no governed path.
- A stored row registered with no package argument but stamped with another namespace's `_packageId` is an unjudged second holder on `main` too. This is not this PR's move; it is a follow-up candidate.

**Must-fix**

   - Measured: alpha and beta become holders, and gamma's extension is orphaned silently.
   - Fix: judge any registration that fills a package's slot (an overlay of the holder's own list adds no holder and passes), and pin it.
2. **R2-C's refusal reaches a production caller** (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts:548`, `bare: engine.resolveFunctionEntry?.(name)` in `releaseMovedFunctions`, from #32468).
   - What moves: a re-bind that moves one function off an owner which also keeps a two-namespace function name. Before: released and held once. Now: the bare read throws 409, teardown aborts with an error log, and the moved function stays held by both owners.
   - Measured: one-holder CONTROL clean.
   - Fix: read the owner's own entry for a name several packages hold, add a runtime pin, and correct row 19 in the body and the changeset.

**Should-fix**
- A refused hot reload still ingests the payload's objects (`plugin.ts:1435-1436`), so row 18's "refused whole" overstates. Skip the ingest on refusal, or reword the row.
- Row 12 moves a one-holder answer with the arm at "—"; give it its narrowing arm.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `caf6941d896ed4f833d24f15b5ecf995ca45be47`
Local-runs: probe — one worktree at the head (closures built with OS_SKIP_DTS=1): the touched suites, four in-place ablations (the `registerItem` provenance skip, the arrival judge skipping tenant-authored lists, the owner-entry read in `releaseMovedFunctions`, the reload ingest skip), uncommitted scratch cases for the round-2 must-fix scenarios and the `registerObject` exclusion, and trial merges of `origin/main` and `origin/claude/project-thread-wqgmuu`
Scope: delta over FAIL 6815437823 at 2386ae1a per epic ruling 6815473607: packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-function-package-scope.test.ts, .changeset/31700-picklist-family-names-per-namespace.md + read for context: packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts

### ① Derived judgments
- **Declarations stand:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, ADR-0087 marker present, `Skills-docs: follow-up #32522`. Size 1980+ / 303−, 35 files, under the 3,000 cap. No `packages/spec` file and no governed path.
- **Round delta:** four dev commits (13 source lines in `registry.ts`, 19 in `plugin.ts`, 15 in `app-artifact-handlers.ts`, pins, changeset) and four merges of `main`. Every merge is clean: the combined diff of each merge commit is empty.
- **Probe at head, all green:**
  - objectql (bare-name one-holder, request family, picklist, boot audit, resolver, hook binder, function registry): 273/273
  - runtime (`app-artifact-handlers.test.ts` and `src/domains`): 5828/5828
  - service-automation, whole package: 3785/3785
  - metadata (loaders, migrations, match-endpoint): 841/841
  - core `package-scoped-resolution.test.ts`: 30/30
  - metadata-protocol dataset-holders: 7/7
- **R3-A holds.**
  - `registry.ts:8191` now reads `type === 'picklist' && packageId`. The round-2 scenario (`registerItem('picklist', { name: 'p1', _provenance: 'org' }, 'name', 'com.acme.beta')` after the seal, alpha holding `p1`, gamma's extension installed) is refused 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Holders stay `[alpha]`, no orphan, alpha's options keep gamma's `extra`.
  - Ablation 1 (the `!isTenantAuthored(item)` skip restored): 1 red, the item-seam pin.
  - Ablation 2 (the pending view skipping tenant-authored lists): 4 red, the install door, `registerApp`, hot reload and the item seam. Each door pin carries a holder-own-overlay CONTROL, green throughout.
  - The one-holder item seam refuses a tenant-authored co-owner for picklist, mapping and dataset, with an own-overlay CONTROL.
- **`registerObject`'s tenant exclusion is sound.** Measured: a tenant-authored object under beta reading `p1` adds no holder, orphans nothing, and resolves caller-less. A tenant-authored `extend` layer under beta that redeclares alpha's field, while beta holds its own `p1`, leaves the field on alpha's list with no disagreement; the same layer without the provenance is refused. `picklistReferrerOf` drops tenant-authored layers, so such a layer fills no package's slot and writes no package's reference. It is not in R3-A's class.
- **R3-B holds.**
  - `releaseMovedFunctions` (`app-artifact-handlers.ts:557`) reads the bare entry only for a one-holder name. The runtime pin (two-holder kept name, one function moved) is green with its one-holder CONTROL.
  - Ablation 3 (the bare read restored): 1 red, the two-holder case; the CONTROL stays green.
  - A repo-wide grep for `resolveFunction` and `resolveFunctionEntry` (all `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `ui/` and examples included) finds one production caller, this one. The flow `script` and screen nodes go through `AutomationEngine.resolveFunction` and `functionHoldersOf`. The hook binder reads `functionHoldersOf(name).packageItem`. Hooks have no bare read. R2-C touched no other type.
- **The service-automation change is test-only** (`c8acabc98`, one test file, 4 lines). The answer it now asserts is row 19's declared 409. See the should-fix on that row's FROM cell.
- **R3-C holds.**
  - A refused reload answers `'refused'` and skips the ingest (`plugin.ts:1437`); the pin asserts the payload's object is not registered. Ablation 4 (the ingest restored): 1 red.
  - Row 12 carries its narrowing arm in the body and the changeset. The changeset states the migration now binds picklist, mapping and dataset rows, and adds `@objectstack/runtime: patch`.
- **CI at this head is not green.** 56 checks success; `Test Core (1/8)` failed on `@objectstack/mcp` `src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts` ("out of CPU budget on the worker"). The PR touches nothing under `packages/mcp`, the file passed 3/3 locally at this head, and `main` at `1a17e96a2` is green. It reads as a timing flake and needs a re-run before any arm.
- **K = 2** behind `origin/main` (`1a17e96a2`). The trial merge is clean (one auto-merge in `app-artifact-handlers.ts`), and runtime `app-artifact-handlers*` is 137/137 on the merged tree. A trial merge of `origin/claude/project-thread-wqgmuu` (PR #32507) conflicts in four files: `packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts`.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on core, metadata, objectql and metadata-protocol is right for `narrowed`. `patch` on runtime is right: the re-bind fix moves no one-holder answer. service-automation needs no bump (test only).

### ③ Boundary flags
- No `packages/spec` file and no governed path.
- Follow-up candidate, not this PR's move: the bare function map is lossy after a holder leaves. Measured: alpha and beta both hold `f`, beta (registered last) is removed, then `resolveFunctionEntry('f')` answers nothing although alpha still holds it. `unregisterFunctionsByPackage` behaves the same on `main`. Two namespaces' package binds make the state newly reachable. The one production reader tolerates it. The dev reported it as out of scope.
- Carried, per ruling R3: a stored row stamped with another namespace's `_packageId` and registered with no package argument stays out of this PR.

### ④ Design judgment
The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at each door, and it holds against the cited code. No must-fix.

**Should-fix**
- **Row 19's FROM cell is wrong for one door** (PR body row 19; `.changeset/31700-picklist-family-names-per-namespace.md:34`).
  - What it says: "(unreachable: the second was refused at bind)".
  - What `main` did: two packages registered through `ObjectQL#registerFunction` directly were both held, and the bare read answered the last registration. `flow-function-package-scope.test.ts:145` pinned that on `main` ("the bare map keeps the last registration"), and it is the line this round changed.
  - Also measured: the refusal fires for any two packages, a same-namespace pair registered directly included (409), while the row and the Clause-② sentence say "two namespaces".
  - The move is declared and pinned (TO, narrowing arm R2-C, three pins). Only the FROM cell and the scope wording are off.
  - Fix: FROM reads "the last registration, through direct `ObjectQL#registerFunction` under two package owners (pinned by #32073's precondition); unreachable through a package bind". Say "two packages" where the code refuses two packages. Body and changeset.

**Nit**
- Row 20's "admitted where row 1 admits" has no pin of its own for a tenant-authored body. Measured admitted for picklist, mapping and dataset (holders become alpha and beta, each package reads its own list).
